value.rationale: The new structural counterexample answers a natural limitation of stability results for adaptive transfer systems: even maximal frozen stochastic mixing, uniformly positive transition entries, a fixed strictly convex quadratic loss and a unique locally attracting equilibrium cannot provide any finite topological-entropy bound for the coupled dynamics. The exact m-branch subshift is a quantitative all-m construction, not simply an arbitrary unnamed chaotic map. It separates plant mixing, stationary equilibrium stability and global deterministic dynamical complexity.
